title: Borrow Rules
story: At a library, many people can read the same book, but only one person can write in it — and nobody else can read while they're writing. XIOM enforces this at compile time.
why: The borrow rules are the foundation of XIOM's memory safety — they guarantee no data races, no dangling pointers, and no iterator invalidation.
analogy: Borrow rules are like a library reading room — any number of people can quietly read, but if someone is updating the catalog, everyone else must wait outside.
try_it: Try to hold a & borrow and create a &mut borrow at the same time. Observe the compiler error and fix it with scoping.
tips: The rule is: many & OR one &mut, never both simultaneously
Use scopes { } to control how long borrows live
The compiler error messages tell you exactly which borrows conflict
These rules are checked at compile time — zero runtime cost
common_mistakes: Trying to mutate through a & reference — use &mut for mutation
Holding a &mut too long — structure code so writes are quick and scoped
Thinking the rules apply at runtime — they're purely compile-time checks
